modules.brief: Read, write, edit and list the files of the workspace.
modules.detail:
Reading is the cheap direction of this sandbox and writing is the expensive one, so a program that reads a dozen files to decide what to change is well shaped, while one that rewrites forty large files in a single turn will exhaust its fuel budget.

Nothing here places anything in the agent's context window. `views::open_file` is the call that does.

modules.brief: Run shell commands in the workspace.
modules.detail:
One function, and the way a program reaches everything gg has no tool for: a build, a test run, `git`, `curl`, a package manager. The workspace is the working directory.

A non-zero exit is a result rather than a failure, because deciding whether a build or a test run passed is the single most common thing a program does with one.

modules.brief: Decompose the work into epics and dispatchable issues.
modules.detail: An issue is the heavyweight unit of work: its scope, non-scope and completion criteria are exactly what a delegated child agent is briefed from, which is why creating one asks for more than adding a task does.

modules.brief: Keep a task list whose entries may wait on each other.
modules.detail: A DAG rather than a list of lines: every task may name the tasks that must finish before it, and an edge that would close a cycle is refused.

modules.brief: Keep durable memories that survive context compaction.
modules.detail:
A run picks one of three memory strategies and binds only that strategy's functions, so what this module offers is the honest answer to what memory can do in a given run. The scratchpad keeps every memory in the context window; the two file-shaped strategies keep the contents outside it, one behind an index that is always in context and one behind a search.

Every mutation hands back the budget after it, so a program decides whether to write another memory by reading numbers rather than by parsing a sentence about them.

modules.brief: Show a file, a value, or a function's documentation in the agent's own context window.
modules.detail: Under responses as code a whole program's output would otherwise collapse into one anonymous blob, charged to one band, attributable to nothing and closable by nothing. A view restores what tool calling gave for free: one message per view, carrying the band it is charged to and the selector it can be closed by.

modules.brief: Find the functions and types this run bound, and take their documentation back out of context.
modules.detail:
Discovery is two steps: `docs::search` answers with one-line briefs, each carrying the fully-qualified name it is keyed by, and `views::open_docs_view` reads one of those names in full. Nothing else names a function — the system prompt lists the modules and stops there.

Searching is bound to every program whatever a run enables, because an agent that cannot find its own surface does not have one. Closing is the exception and is bought by a capability: opening documentation only ever adds to the end of the prompt, while closing it rewrites the middle.

modules.brief: Reclaim room in the agent's own context window.
modules.detail: These are the only calls whose effect is on the conversation rather than on the workspace, and they are worth making from a program precisely because a program can decide when to: read a set of files, extract what matters, then evict the views, all in one turn.

modules.brief: Delegate work to child agents, and hand this session on to another agent.
modules.detail: Waiting can dominate a turn's wall clock, because it blocks while real agents run and the run's budget keeps ticking, so a program spawns broadly and waits once rather than spawning and waiting in a loop.

modules.brief: Read the skills this run was given.
modules.detail: A skill name is a plain string rather than an enumerator, because the catalogue is per run while this SDK is compiled once. The system prompt lists the names available, and an unknown one comes back as `not_found` carrying the full list.

modules.brief: Fetch a program that already ran, and hand a patched copy back to be run.
End this session, in the shape the agent's own role ends one.
modules.detail:
Under responses as code every reply is a program, so there is no prose turn that could mean "I am done": a model that answers "task complete" has written a reply that failed to be a program rather than an ending. These are the calls that mean it, and an agent is bound the one its role uses — an agent doing work ends by reporting what it did, and a reviewer ends with a verdict.

None of them stops the program: whatever follows still runs, so an ending belongs last, once the work is confirmed done. A program that then fails cancels the ending and earns another turn.

modules.brief: The types every other module's signatures name: how a call fails, and how it is classified.
modules.detail: It declares no capability of its own: a program reaches `core::tool_error` by catching one, and `core::tool_error_code` by branching on the failure it caught.

functions.name: read_file
functions.brief: Read a file, as either a `files::text_file` or a `files::image_file`.
functions.detail:
Which of the two comes back is detected from the file's bytes, never from the extension, so a mislabelled picture is still a picture. A relative path resolves against the workspace; an absolute one is read as given, so anything else in this container — an offloaded command's output under `/tmp/gg-shell`, say — is readable.

This call hands bytes to the program and places nothing in the context window. Reading a picture describes it and shows nothing, so a file only read here is a file nobody has looked at; `views::open_file` is the one call that shows one.

Returns: the file's text window, or the picture's description.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for a missing path.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to read, relative to the workspace or absolute.

parameters.name: window
parameters.doc: The lines to read; `{}` reads the whole file.

functions.name: read_text_file
functions.brief: Read a text file and hand back its contents directly, without the narrowing.
functions.detail:
It takes the same window as `files::read_file` and is the shape a program wants whenever the path is known to be text.

Returns: the file's text.
Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` when the path names a picture, which `files::read_file` describes and `views::open_file` shows.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to read, relative to the workspace or absolute.

parameters.name: window
parameters.doc: The lines to read; `{}` reads the whole file.

functions.name: write_file
functions.brief: Write UTF-8 text to a file, creating parent directories and replacing whatever was there.
functions.detail:
Writing is the expensive direction of this sandbox: rewriting more than a few dozen large files in one program exhausts its fuel budget, so a large rewrite is split across several turns.

Returns: how many bytes were written.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: Where to write, relative to the workspace or absolute. Parent directories are created.

parameters.name: contents
parameters.doc: The UTF-8 text to write. It replaces the file entirely.

functions.name: edit_file
functions.brief: Replace the one exact occurrence of `old_string` in a file with `new_string`.
functions.detail:
Widening the surrounding text until the match is unique is the way to reach a repeated line, rather than counting occurrences.

Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` when the text does not appear, and `conflict` — with the number of matches — when it appears more than once.

signatures.signature: edit_file(std::string_view path, std::string_view old_string, std::string_view new_string) -> void

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to edit.

parameters.name: old_string
parameters.doc: The exact text to find, whitespace included. It must appear exactly once.

parameters.name: new_string
parameters.doc: The text to put in its place. An empty string deletes the match.

functions.name: list_dir
functions.brief: List a directory, sorted by name; leaving the path out lists the workspace root.
functions.detail:
Each entry carries a bare `name`, which joins with the listed directory, and its `kind`. An empty directory is an empty vector rather than a failure.

Returns: the directory's entries, sorted by name.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The directory to list, relative to the workspace or absolute; empty lists the workspace root.

functions.name: run
functions.brief: Run a command with `sh -c` in the workspace and hand back its merged stdout and stderr.
functions.detail:
A non-zero exit is not a failure: it arrives as `exit_code` on the result, and only a process that could not be launched, or one the timeout killed, throws.

A run may offload shell output, and the `shell` tool's own description says which mode is in force. Under `offload`, `output` holds only the tail that fits and ends with a note naming the two files the command's full stdout and stderr were written to. Under `adaptive`, the default, a command that succeeded returns that note alone and one that failed returns the tail. Grepping the named files is cheaper than running the command again.

Returns: what the process reported when it finished.
Throws: core::tool_error `limit_exceeded` when the timeout killed the process, and `io_error` when it could not be launched.

signatures.signature: run(std::string_view command, std::optional<double> timeout_secs = std::nullopt) -> shell::shell_output

parameters.name: command
parameters.doc: The command line, run by `sh -c` with the workspace as its working directory.

parameters.name: timeout_secs
parameters.doc: How long to let it run before it is killed; empty takes gg's default of 120, clamped to whatever is left of the run's wall-clock budget.

functions.name: create_epic
functions.brief: Create an epic to group related issues, and hand back its id and the board budget.
functions.detail:
The prefix is upper-cased and becomes the epic's id, which is also the stem its issues are numbered from: a prefix of `auth` gives issues `AUTH-1`, `AUTH-2`, and so on.

Returns: the id the prefix resolved to, and the board budget.
Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` when the prefix is not 3-6 letters, and `conflict` when another epic already holds it.

signatures.signature: create_epic(std::string_view prefix, std::string_view title, std::string_view description) -> board::epic_created

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.doc: 3-6 letters naming it. Upper-cased, it becomes the epic's id.

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: A short line naming the body of work.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: What the epic covers, for a reader who has not seen its issues.

functions.name: create_issue
functions.brief: Create a self-contained, dispatchable issue, and hand back the id the board assigned it.
functions.detail:
The id is numbered under its epic's prefix (`AUTH-1`), or under `ISSUE` when the issue has no epic, and the board rather than the caller chooses it — so the returned one is what blocks a later issue on this one or waits for it. The scope, non-scope and completion criteria are what a child agent is briefed from, so they are written for a reader with no other context.

Returns: the id the board assigned, and the board budget.
Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` when the agent or a reviewer is not one this agent may assign, and `conflict` on a blocker edge that would close a cycle.

signatures.signature: create_issue(std::string_view title, std::string_view in_scope, std::string_view out_of_scope, std::string_view completion_criteria, std::string_view agent, board::issue_options options = {}) -> board::issue_created

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: A short line naming the work.

parameters.name: in_scope
parameters.doc: What the issue covers, precisely. Part of the brief a child agent is given.

parameters.name: out_of_scope
parameters.doc: What the issue deliberately does not cover, so the work stops where it was meant to.

parameters.name: completion_criteria
parameters.doc: What must be true for the issue to be done, which is what a reviewer checks the work against.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent the issue is dispatched to. It must be one this agent may spawn.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: The parts that may be left out: a description, blockers, an epic, reviewers.

functions.name: update_issue
functions.brief: Revise an issue; at least one field of the patch is required.
functions.detail:
A field left at its default is left alone, `tasks::text_edit::clear()` empties the description, and `board::epic_assignment::ungroup()` detaches the issue from its epic.

Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue to revise.

parameters.name: patch
parameters.doc: The fields to change. At least one is required; a field left at its default is left alone.

functions.name: set_issue_blocked_by
functions.brief: Replace an issue's whole blocker set; an empty vector clears every blocker.
functions.detail: Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id, and `conflict` when an edge would close a cycle.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue whose blockers to replace.

parameters.name: blocked_by
parameters.doc: The ids of every issue that must now be done before it.

functions.name: remove_epic
functions.brief: Remove an epic, keeping its issues and ungrouping them, and hand back the board budget.
functions.detail:
Returns: how much of the board budget is left in use.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The epic to remove.

functions.name: remove_issue
functions.brief: Remove an issue and every blocker edge pointing at it, and hand back the board budget.
functions.detail:
Returns: how much of the board budget is left in use.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue to remove.

functions.name: wait_for_issue
functions.brief: Register a wait on an issue and hand back an acknowledgement.
functions.detail:
It does not block inside the program: it records the wait and returns at once, so the rest of the program still runs and the suspension happens after the program ends, between turns. The run then frees this agent's slot for others until the issue is terminal — done, or failed because its assigned agent could not complete it — and resumes on the next turn. The issue this agent was assigned to implement cannot be waited on.

Returns: gg's acknowledgement of the registered wait.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue to wait on. It may not be the issue this agent was assigned.

functions.name: add_task
functions.brief: Add a task to the task DAG and hand back the task budget.
functions.detail:
`options.blocked_by` names the tasks that must finish before this one, and defaults to none.

Returns: how much of the task budget is used.
Throws: core::tool_error `conflict` on a duplicate id or on an edge that would close a cycle.

signatures.signature: add_task(std::string_view id, std::string_view title, tasks::task_options options = {}) -> tasks::task_usage

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The id to file it under. Every other task call takes it, and no two tasks may share one.

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: A short line naming the work.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: The parts that may be left out: a description, and the tasks this one waits on.

functions.name: update_task
functions.brief: Revise a task's title, description or status; at least one of the three is required.
functions.detail:
A field left at its default is left alone, `tasks::text_edit::clear()` empties the description, and `tasks::text_edit::set(…)` replaces it.

Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The task to revise.

parameters.name: patch
parameters.doc: The fields to change. At least one is required; a field left at its default is left alone.

functions.name: set_blocked_by
functions.brief: Replace a task's whole blocker set; an empty vector clears every blocker.
functions.detail: Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id, and `conflict` when an edge would close a cycle.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The task whose blockers to replace.

parameters.name: blocked_by
parameters.doc: The ids of every task that must now be done before it.

functions.name: complete_task
functions.brief: Mark a task done, which makes the tasks it was blocking actionable.
functions.detail:
A blocked task becomes actionable once every one of its blockers is done, not merely this one.

Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The task to mark done.

functions.name: remove_task
functions.brief: Remove a task and every blocker edge pointing at it, and hand back the task budget.
functions.detail:
Returns: how much of the task budget is left in use.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The task to remove.

functions.name: write_memory
functions.brief: Record a durable memory that survives context compaction, and hand back the memory budget.
functions.detail:
A memory may also carry code: `options.code` is a C++ translation unit whose declarations are bound at `lib::<name>` in every later program, so a helper written correctly once is never written again, and `options.on_use` is a program gg runs the first time the memory comes into use. Neither costs any context window.

Returns: how much of the memory budget is now used.
Throws: core::tool_error `conflict` on a duplicate name, and `limit_exceeded` when the body would breach the run's caps.

signatures.signature: write_memory(std::string_view name, std::string_view description, std::string_view body, memories::memory_options options = {}) -> memories::memory_usage

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory's slug: letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`. Every other memory call takes it, and no two memories may share one.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: One line saying what the memory holds. Where the run keeps an index, this is the memory's line in it.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: The memory's contents.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: The code halves, which may be left out.

functions.name: update_memory
functions.brief: Replace an existing memory's description and body, keyed on its slug.
functions.detail:
Its code and on-use program are replaced too, so leaving them out of `options` clears the ones the memory had.

Returns: how much of the memory budget is now used.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` when no memory has that name.

signatures.signature: update_memory(std::string_view name, std::string_view description, std::string_view body, memories::memory_options options = {}) -> memories::memory_usage

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The slug of the memory to replace.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: The one-line description to replace the old one with.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: The contents to replace the old ones with.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: The code halves. Leaving one out clears the one the memory had.

functions.name: create_memory
functions.brief: Record a new memory whose contents stay out of the context window until they are read.
functions.detail:
This is the file-shaped strategies' write: the description is what the index carries, and it is required where the run keeps one, because it is all that is seen of the memory until it is read.

Returns: how much of the memory budget is now used.
Throws: core::tool_error `conflict` on a duplicate slug, and `limit_exceeded` when the contents or the index entry would breach a limit.

signatures.signature: create_memory(std::string_view name, std::string_view description, std::string_view body, memories::memory_options options = {}) -> memories::memory_usage

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory's slug: letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: One line saying what the memory holds, which is its line in the index.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: The memory's initial contents, which stay out of the context window until they are read.

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: The code halves, which load on that first read.

functions.name: read_memory
functions.brief: Read one memory's full contents by slug, which is the only thing that brings them into context.
functions.detail:
A memory carrying code loads it on this read: the reply names the `lib::<key>` it is bound at, and it stays bound for the rest of the session.

Returns: the memory's full contents.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` when no memory has that slug.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory's slug.

functions.name: edit_memory
functions.brief: Revise a memory in place, replacing the one exact occurrence of `search` with `replace`.
functions.detail:
Appending is quoting the last line and replacing it with itself plus what is being added.

Returns: how much of the memory budget is now used.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` when the text does not appear, `conflict` when it appears more than once, `limit_exceeded` when the result would be too long, and `invalid_argument` when the edit would leave the memory empty.

signatures.signature: edit_memory(std::string_view name, std::string_view search, std::string_view replace) -> memories::memory_usage

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The slug of the memory to revise.

parameters.name: search
parameters.doc: The exact text to find in its contents. It must appear exactly once.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.doc: The text to put in its place.

functions.name: search_memories
functions.brief: Find the memories mentioning any of `keywords`, best first.
functions.detail:
Plain case-insensitive substring matching over each memory's slug, description and contents, ranked by how many distinct keywords a memory mentions and then by how often. Several specific words rank better than one sentence, and a search that matches nothing is an empty vector rather than a failure.

Returns: the memories that matched, best first.
Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` when every keyword is empty.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.doc: The words to look for. Several specific words rank better than one sentence.

functions.name: delete_memory
functions.brief: Evict a memory by slug, freeing room in the budget.
functions.detail:
Returns: how much of the memory budget is left in use.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` when no memory has that name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory's slug.

functions.name: open_file
functions.brief: Read a file and show it, so the program gets the bytes and the context window gets the file.
functions.detail:
The split from `files::read_file` is the point: that call gets bytes for the program, this one shows a file to the agent, so a program that reads forty files to grep them still puts nothing in the window. Two pages of one file are two views that coexist, and re-opening the same page replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate. An image is shown as a picture, and this is the only call that shows one.

Re-opening a picture that is already open replaces it rather than adding a second copy, which is the same rule a page of a file follows.

Returns: the same read `files::read_file` would have handed back.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for a missing path, and `invalid_argument` for an offset past the end of the file. The read is what fails; nothing is opened when it does.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to open, relative to the workspace or absolute.

parameters.name: window
parameters.doc: The lines to show; `{}` shows the whole file.

functions.name: open_text
functions.brief: Show a value the program computed, filed under `label`.
functions.detail:
A directory listing, a command's output, a child agent's answer and an assembled table are all this. Opening the same label again replaces what it showed, so a program may refine a view in a loop without piling up a copy per iteration.

Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` for an empty label — a view with no selector could never be closed or attributed — and `limit_exceeded`, naming the cap, for a body or label over gg's caps.

parameters.name: label
parameters.doc: What to file the view under. Closing it takes this, and opening the same label again replaces what it showed. It may not be empty.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: What to show. An empty body is allowed: it is how something that was being shown is said to be empty now.

functions.name: open_docs_view
functions.brief: Show the full documentation for one function: its signature, its description, and its types.
functions.detail:
A type is declared once per session, so what arrives is the declarations of the types this function refers to that have not been shown already. It is a view rather than a return value — the documentation arrives in the next prompt under a `Documentation` heading, exactly as a file or a computed value does — so it is not available in the turn it is asked for: ask in one turn, use it in the next. Opening the same function's documentation again replaces the view rather than adding a second copy.

Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown or unbound name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The function to document, by the fully-qualified name its documentation is keyed by — `"gg::files::read_file"`. The bare name it is called under its module (`"read_file"`) also resolves and is a fallback rather than the form to reach for: two modules are free to declare a `close`, and only the qualified name says which one is meant. Searching the documentation is what says which names exist.

functions.name: close
functions.brief: Close every view carrying `selector`, freeing the tokens they occupied.
functions.detail:
For a file that is every page of that path, for a text view the one with that label, and for the results of a search the label `search results`. Closing a selector that is not open hands back `0` rather than failing, so a program that tidies up unconditionally needs no guard. Closing a file view forgets what was read rather than what exists; closing a text view discards the only copy of what it held.

Documentation views are not reached from here. `docs::close` is what takes one away, and it is bought by a capability this call is not — so a sweep that included them would hand back `0` for an agent that may not close one, which reads as a selector that named nothing.

Returns: how many views were closed.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.doc: What the view is filed under: a file's path, a text view's label, or `search results`.

functions.name: current
functions.brief: List what is open in the context window right now, with what each one costs.
functions.detail:
Each entry carries its `kind`, the `selector` that closes it, roughly what it costs in `tokens`, and — for a paged file view — the `region` it covers. What it enumerates is the context window's contents, not any module's functions.

Returns: every view open in the context window right now.

functions.name: search
functions.brief: Search the bound functions and types by keyword, by module, or by both — best match first.
functions.detail:
Matching is case-insensitive substring over names, signatures, briefs and detailed descriptions, so `docs` finds `open_docs_view` and `view` finds every call that mentions one. Ranking is by the kind of evidence that matched: an entry whose own name matched outranks one that merely mentions the word in a paragraph, however often it mentions it. Only what this run bound is ever returned, so nothing a search finds is something the program cannot call.

The result is a value and a view. The value is readable in the turn that asked for it; the view puts the same page in the next prompt under the selector `search results`, replaced by the next search rather than accumulating, and closed by `views::close`. A hit carries a brief and no more — reading one in full is `views::open_docs_view` on its `key`.

Returns: the page that matched, best first, and how many matched behind it.
Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` when `query` is empty and no filter is set — asking for nothing and matching nothing are different answers — and when `limit` is `0`, which is a page that could never answer anything.

parameters.name: query
parameters.doc: The words to look for, matched as case-insensitive substrings. Several specific words rank an entry above one vague word. It may be empty when `filters` narrows the search.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.doc: The filters and the page; `{}` searches the whole bound surface and takes the first page.

functions.name: close
functions.brief: Take one documentation view out of the context window, by the key it was opened under.
functions.detail:
The removal does not cascade: closing a function's view leaves the views of the types it named, and closing a type's leaves every function beside it, because nothing records why a view was opened. A type closed here is opened again by the next function that mentions it.

Returns: how many views were closed, which is `0` when that key is not open — not a failure, so a program that tidies up unconditionally needs no guard.
Throws: core::tool_error `unavailable` when this agent was not given the capability that buys closing documentation.

parameters.name: key
parameters.doc: The fully-qualified name the view was opened under, as a hit's `key` reports it.

functions.name: close_all
functions.brief: Take every documentation view out of the context window, and report how many went.
functions.detail:
The blanket form of `docs::close`, on the same terms and behind the same capability: what it frees is every documentation view the session has opened, and none of the file or text views beside them.

Returns: how many views were closed.
Throws: core::tool_error `unavailable` when this agent was not given the capability that buys closing documentation.

functions.name: evict_file_view
functions.brief: Drop the contents of files that were read out of the context window.
functions.detail:
The files on disk are untouched: this forgets what was read, not what exists.

Returns: what the reclaim actually freed.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file whose views to drop; empty drops every file view the agent holds.

functions.name: archive_thread
functions.brief: Move whole turns out of the context window, keeping their results searchable.
functions.detail:
Every result carries a header with its turn number and roughly what holding it costs, which is what names the turns worth dropping. Both ends of a span are included, so `context::archive_thread({{4, 19}})` archives turns 4 through 19. The agent's own messages in an archived turn are dropped; the results are kept and stay searchable.

Returns: what the archive actually freed.
Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` for a span whose ends are not turn numbers.

parameters.name: ranges
parameters.doc: The inclusive spans of turn numbers to move out of the window. They may overlap.

functions.name: search_archive
functions.brief: Search archived history for a case-insensitive substring, most recent first, up to 8 hits.
functions.detail:
Reading `archive_empty` before `hits` is what tells "nothing has been archived yet" from "the search ran and matched nothing".

Returns: whether anything is archived at all, and the matches.

parameters.name: query
parameters.doc: The substring to look for. Matching is case-insensitive.

functions.name: compact
functions.brief: Compact the context window: the detailed thread is dropped and restarted from `summary`.
functions.detail:
Each path in `files` is read afresh into the restarted window, and the agent's skills, memories and task list are kept as they are. gg asks for this call when the window is full, and refuses every other call until it arrives.

It does not stop the program: it registers the request and returns, and the rewrite happens once the program has ended. Everything not in the summary and not in `files` is gone afterwards.

Throws: core::tool_error `refused` when a compaction is already in flight and this call is not the one it asked for.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: What the restarted window opens with. Everything not in it and not re-read from `files` is gone.

parameters.name: files
parameters.doc: The paths to read afresh into the restarted window. An empty vector reads nothing back.

functions.name: spawn_subagent
functions.brief: Delegate scoped work to a child agent and hand back its handle immediately.
functions.detail:
The child runs in parallel while the program continues, and shares the workspace. The agent profile selects its model, its tools and its instructions, and the system prompt lists the ones this agent may spawn.

Returns: the child's handle, for waiting on it or messaging it.
Throws: core::tool_error `limit_exceeded` at the delegation depth cap, and `invalid_argument` for an agent this agent may not spawn.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent profile to run the child as, from the ones this agent may spawn.

parameters.name: task
parameters.doc: What the child is to do: `delegation::brief::prompt` with self-contained instructions, or `delegation::brief::issue` with a board issue's id.

functions.name: wait_for_subagents
functions.brief: Block until the named children have finished, and collect their results in dispatch order.
functions.detail:
Called with no arguments at all it waits for every child still outstanding, which is the usual shape: the run's wall-clock budget keeps running throughout, so one wait for many children costs less than one wait per child.

Returns: one result per named child, in dispatch order.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.doc: The children to wait for, as spawning them returned their handles.

functions.name: send_message
functions.brief: Deliver a message to a running child agent's inbox, which it reads at its next turn.
functions.detail: Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` for an unknown agent id, and `conflict` when that child has already returned.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.doc: The child to deliver to, as spawning it returned its handle.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to put in its inbox.

functions.name: transition_state
functions.brief: Move the process this agent is running inside on to another of its states.
functions.detail:
It is bound only when a state machine is driving the agent and the current state has somewhere to go. Like a compaction it is registered rather than performed: the call validates the target and returns, the program runs on to its end, and the transition happens after that — replacing the agent, and its window, mid-program would pull every remaining call out from under it. The first declaration in a turn stands.

Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` for a state this agent may not move to, and `refused` for a second declaration in one turn.

signatures.signature: transition_state(std::string_view state, std::optional<std::string_view> note = std::nullopt) -> void

parameters.name: state
parameters.doc: The state to move on to, named the way an agent to spawn is named.

parameters.name: note
parameters.doc: The opening message the next state's agent sees; empty tells it nothing.

functions.name: exec
functions.brief: Continue this session as a different agent from the next turn on.
functions.detail:
The named agent takes over with its own model, tools and instructions, keeping every capability the two of them share — the whole conversation above all, so it needs no catching up. Registered rather than performed, exactly as a state transition is and for the same reason, and a session makes one succession per turn. It is bound only for an agent that may make agent transitions and has agents it may become, and never while a state machine is driving it.

Throws: core::tool_error `invalid_argument` for an agent this agent may not become, and `refused` for a second succession in one turn.

signatures.signature: exec(std::string_view agent, std::optional<std::string_view> prompt = std::nullopt) -> void

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to become, from the ones this agent may become.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: Its opening message. It already has the whole conversation, so this is the instruction rather than a briefing; empty tells it nothing.

functions.name: fork
functions.brief: Run a copy of this agent, in parallel, on something it will not do itself.
functions.detail:
The copy has the same model, the same tools and a private copy of the whole conversation, so the prompt is the difference rather than a briefing. Its handle comes back immediately, but the copy starts once this turn's results are recorded — the conversation it inherits has to be a complete one — so it can only be collected on a later turn and never in the program that made it.

Returns: the copy's handle.
Throws: core::tool_error `limit_exceeded` at the delegation depth cap.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: What the copy is to do instead. It has the whole conversation already, so this is the difference rather than a briefing.

functions.name: read_skill
functions.brief: Read a skill by name, which also pins its body permanently into the context window.
functions.detail:
The body comes back with its front matter stripped. A skill may be code rather than prose, or as well as it: code is bound at `lib::<key>` for the rest of the session and the reply names the key and what it offers, and an on-use program runs once this program has ended, with whatever it shows arriving on the next turn.

Returns: the skill's body, with its front matter stripped.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found`, listing the skills that do exist, when the name is unknown.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The skill's name, as the system prompt lists it.

functions.name: history
functions.brief: List the programs this session has already run, oldest first.
functions.detail:
It lists shapes rather than sources, so fetching the one worth having is a second call. The list survives a compaction, which is what makes it the way to find a program whose text has left the context window, and it is empty rather than an error for a session that has run nothing yet.

Returns: one summary per program this session has run, oldest first.

functions.name: get
functions.brief: Fetch the exact source of one program that ran; with no argument, the most recent one.
functions.detail:
This is the first half of fixing a program without rewriting it: fetch what ran, patch it with ordinary string work, and hand the result back to be run. What comes back is the program that executed — so where a turn's program was itself handed over, this is the program that ran rather than the few lines that asked for it, and fetch-patch-run composes turn after turn.

Returns: that program's exact source.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found`, naming the turns that are held, for a turn that ran no program or one old enough that the library has dropped it.

parameters.name: turn
parameters.doc: The turn whose program to fetch, as the history reports it; empty fetches the most recent one.

functions.name: rerun
functions.brief: Hand gg a program to run in place of this one, once this one has finished.
functions.detail:
Nothing is undone: every call this program already made stands, and the program that runs next sees the world this one left behind — so the hand-over belongs before work that should not happen twice. The first call in a turn stands, because a silently replaced program is a change nobody can see, and a program that then fails cancels the hand-over along with everything else it decided.

Throws: core::tool_error `refused` for a second hand-over in one turn, and `invalid_argument` for a blank source.

parameters.name: source
parameters.doc: The program to run in place of this one, as C++. It may not be blank, and it must define `main`.

functions.name: finish
functions.brief: End this session, reporting what was done in a sentence or two.
functions.detail:
It is the only thing that ends a working agent's session, and it does not stop the program: whatever follows it still runs, so it belongs last, once the tools have confirmed the work is really done.

Throws: core::tool_error `unavailable` when this agent's role does not end this way, and `invalid_argument` for an empty summary.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: What was done, in a sentence or two.

functions.name: approve
functions.brief: Accept the work under review: it meets every completion criterion and stays in scope.
functions.detail:
It ends the reviewing session and takes nothing, because an approval carries no obligation beyond itself. It does not stop the program, so it belongs after the change has actually been read.

Throws: core::tool_error `unavailable` when this agent's role is not to review.

functions.name: request_changes
functions.brief: Reject the work under review, listing every change that must be made before it can stand.
functions.detail:
It ends the reviewing session and does not stop the program. Each item says what is wrong and what to change, and the list may not be empty.

Throws: core::tool_error `unavailable` when this agent's role is not to review, and `invalid_argument` when the list is empty.

parameters.name: items
parameters.doc: Every change that must be made before the work can be accepted, one per entry. It may not be empty.

functions.name: wait
functions.brief: Register a wait on this issue, which suspends the agent between turns until it is terminal.
functions.detail:
Returns: gg's acknowledgement of the registered wait.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` when the issue has since been removed.

functions.name: read
functions.brief: Read this memory's full contents, which is the only thing that brings them into context.
functions.detail:
Returns: the memory's full contents.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` when the memory has since been deleted.

functions.name: close
functions.brief: Close this view, freeing the tokens it occupied.
functions.detail:
A documentation view is the one this does not take away, because `views::close` does not reach that band: `docs::close(selector)` is the call for one of those.

Returns: how many views were closed, which is `0` when it has been closed already.

functions.name: send
functions.brief: Deliver a message to this child's inbox, which it reads at its next turn.
functions.detail: Throws: core::tool_error `conflict` when this child has already returned.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to put in its inbox.

functions.name: source
functions.brief: Fetch the exact source of this program.
functions.detail:
Returns: that program's exact source.
Throws: core::tool_error `not_found` when the library has since dropped that turn.

types.brief: A three-way edit of an optional text field: leave it, empty it, or replace it.
types.detail: The field really has three states and an `std::optional<std::string>` could say only two of them, which is how a stringly interface ends up treating "clear it" and "set it to the empty string" as one request. A default-constructed value keeps the field, so a patch that says nothing about a description leaves it alone. `board::update_issue` takes the same type for the same reason.
